guesses.reason: The fluffy, mostly white coat, sturdy puppy build, and tan-to-gray 'badger' head markings with a white blaze are classic for Great Pyrenees or Pyrenees-mix puppies.
The blue-gray puppy eyes, soft medium-length fur, and copper face markings with dark ear shading hint at herding-breed ancestry.
The symmetrical brown head patch split by a white muzzle and blaze, plus the broad puppy face, resemble Saint Bernard facial markings.

breed.appearance: A fluffy young puppy with a mostly white, medium-length coat on the body, legs, chest, and muzzle, and a symmetrical golden-tan 'hood' over both ears and around the eyes, split by a white blaze down the forehead. The soft folded ears are tan with darker sooty-black shading toward the tips, and there are faint dark patches around the eyes. The eyes are almond-shaped and blue-gray, the nose is black, and a tiny pink tongue tip peeks out as the puppy lies on a stone ledge with its white front paws stretched forward.
breed.fun_fact: Great Pyrenees are gentle giants bred to guard flocks, so they are famously calm, loyal, and protective of their families!
